sections.what_happened: Macron opened his Gulf tour Monday (Kuwait first; UAE, Bahrain, Qatar next) after nearly staying home over violent protests in France (school-conditions/cost-of-living unrest). Elysee: talks on securing shipping lanes and 'alternative and bypass routes for liquid hydrocarbons'; G7 (France chair) drew up to 100M barrels from strategic reserves in early Oct. Saudi Arabia NOT on the itinerary ('ongoing contact' only). FM Jean-Noel Barrot traveled to Riyadh Sunday evening to reaffirm solidarity and support for Saudi territorial defense; visited the French woman injured in the Oct 10 Riyadh airport attack (13 dead, 309 injured). France + Britain have assembled an international mission to reopen Hormuz — mainly demining — once US and Iran agree on the waterway. France deployed Charles de Gaulle carrier group in spring + air defenses to Yanbu last month.
sections.what_verified: New Indian Express, Modern Ghana, Minute Mirror (crawled <1h ago) — consistent on itinerary, protests, demining mission, Barrot Riyadh visit. The National (Oct 15) corroborates France/UK/Italy military support + EU-Gulf Riyadh summit postponed from Oct 24.
sections.what_disputed: Energy expert Francis Perrin (IRIS): does not expect the visit to move fuel prices — Gulf states can't commit until the region stabilizes. 'Bypass routes' discussion is aspirational; no concrete deliverable announced.
sections.why_matters: While Washington weighs bombs, Paris sends deminers. Macron skipped Riyadh but wants Gulf fuel — Europe is preparing to clear Hormuz’s mines the day the guns stop. Who really controls the strait: the US Navy, Iran’s mines, or the men who will sweep them?
sections.context: Background: Macron Gulf tour BEGUN Monday — fuel-security tour (UAE/Bahrain/Kuwait/Qatar, Saudi skipped); Barrot in Riyadh; France+UK Hormuz demining mission on standby

totw_analysis: Our read: While Washington weighs bombs, Paris sends deminers. Macron skipped Riyadh but wants Gulf fuel — Europe is preparing to clear Hormuz’s mines the day the guns stop. Who really controls the strait: the US Navy, Iran’s mines, or the men who will sweep them? The fault line our audience is arguing over: Europe’s demining gambit: real contribution to reopening Hormuz, or Macron fuel-shopping theater while Paris riots over the cost of living?
